gloss: to stretch, to enlarge, to delay

definitions.explanation: To pull something to make it longer or larger.
To make a photograph larger, to print an enlargement.
To stretch out the time of something, to drag out a process.

examples.japanese: ゴムを{引|ひ}き{伸|の}ばす。
この{写真|しゃしん}をA4サイズに{引|ひ}き{伸|の}ばしてください。
examples.english: Please enlarge this photo to A4 size.

examples.japanese: {交渉|こうしょう}を{引|ひ}き{伸|の}ばして{時間|じかん}を{稼|かせ}いだ。
examples.english: We bought time by dragging out the negotiations.

notes:
COMPOUND VERB: {引|ひ}く (to pull) + {伸|の}ばす (to extend) = to pull and extend

TRANSITIVITY: Transitive. The intransitive counterpart is {引|ひ}き{伸|の}びる.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{写真|しゃしん}を{引|ひ}き{伸|の}ばす (to enlarge a photo)
・{期間|きかん}を{引|ひ}き{伸|の}ばす (to extend the period)
・{決定|けってい}を{引|ひ}き{伸|の}ばす (to delay a decision)
・{引|ひ}き{伸|の}ばし (noun form: enlargement; delay)

PHOTOGRAPHY USAGE: In the context of film photography, {引|ひ}き{伸|の}ばす refers to making an enlargement print from a negative.

RELATED ～{伸|の}ばす COMPOUND VERBS:
・{書|か}き{伸|の}ばす - to extend in writing
・{押|お}し{伸|の}ばす - to spread by pressing
